_comment: Starter selection document for codebase-organism's refactor/cmd/plan:
This is NOT a triaged plan. It carries forward the rules that four executed waves
already established, plus the two suppressions this directory's areas argue for.
Everything else is still untriaged, and `plan` will stamp "triaged": false until a
real judgement pass exists. Allow lists restrict first; deny lists remove after.
Edit allow_issues to scope a wave to ONE class -- one class per wave keeps a
_deny_paths_why: The twin binary imports no harmonik package at all, which is what makes every one
of its 156 literals a cross-package finding. There is a standing argument that the
decoupling is deliberate: a test twin that imported the code under test would stop
being an independent check of the wire format. Carried forward from the first
executed wave (../report.md). Overturn this deliberately or not at all.
_deny_findings_why: NOTE: these two line numbers are from the 2026-08-04 wave and the schema has no
stable finding id -- `plan` synthesises issue@file:line, which survives re-detection
only while the line has not moved. Re-verify against a fresh findings.json before
The original judgement: the CONSUMER sites for "agent_input_acked" and
"agent_input_stale" would make internal/core -- 48 dependents, no dependencies,
D = 0.98 -- import a leaf package. Area 2 argues the DECLARATION-side literals
inside internal/core itself do not share that objection and should be fixed.
_not_yet_expressible: Three suppressions these areas argue for that this schema cannot state today:
1. A2 struct tags (233 values / 1,913 sites). Not fixable in Go -- tags must be
compile-time literals. The right fix is in the detector (area 8, item 4), not
here; a deny list of 233 values would be a workaround that hides a defect.
2. A1's ambiguous bucket (724 findings, 53% of the class). These need a per-site
human decision about which of two vocabularies the site means. There is no
'defer for judgement' state -- a finding is either work or it is denied, and
3. A2 findings naming more than one file (550 of 653). Unsafe to schedule until
Finding carries files[] (area 8, item 1). Denying them all would be honest but
would empty the class; restricting a wave to one A2 op at a time is the
workaround, and the scheduler has no way to be told that.
